description: Non-blind development cases for the glass-family and II-VI semiconductor failure families exposed by the Q2 diagnostic run. This file may be used for scorer development and must not be reported as blind validation.
selection_policy: Near-neighbor source-backed examples for family-specific rules; Q2 blind pair identities remain in the frozen external file.

pairs.citation: Shelby, Introduction to Glass Science and Technology, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Borosilicate is a silica-network glass family and should not be treated like a crystalline ceramic mismatch under ambient contact context.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Silica and magnesia can react to form magnesium silicates and have severe CTE mismatch.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 4, Ceramics and Glasses; glass-to-glass seal CTE guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 4, Ceramics and Glasses, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Silica-network family similarity alone is not enough for direct seal viability when CTE mismatch is high.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: HgCdTe/CdTe is a standard same-family II-VI infrared detector material pairing.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: Same-family zincblende II-VI materials can be used in buffered optoelectronic heterostructure contexts even when coherent epitaxy is not implied.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: II-VI family membership alone should not override large structural and lattice mismatch.
